messages:
From: Akash Singh <akash.singh@infracorp.com>

Cc: emily@datametric.io
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2029 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Private cluster intake — network & storage constraints at DataMetric

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We ran the internal review and want to move forward with a Private deployment (on our colo rack) — we need help validating network topology, connectivity constraints, and persistent storage options before we lock dates with our data center team.

High-level constraints:
- No outbound internet from the cluster except via a NAT in our perimeter VPC (we can allow specific egress IPs)
- VLANs are strict — management, control-plane, and workloads must be isolated (we have two top-of-rack switches)
- On-prem storage is LUN-backed with iSCSI and a small NVMe shelf for local caching
- We want 3 availability racks (physical failure domains) and the ability to drain a rack without >2 hours of degraded performance

Can you provide a quick checklist of what Redwood needs from our side (CIDR ranges, BGP peers, NAT egress IPs, storage QoS) and a mutual action plan so we can align schedule with the colo vendor? I attached our network diagram (first pass).

Best,
Akash
Site Reliability Lead — InfraCorp

Attachment: infracorp_network_topology_v1.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Akash — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram. Shared below is a prioritized intake checklist and a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so we can lock milestones. Marissa (Solutions) and Neha (Deploy lead) are looped for technical validation and to own the runbook items.

Quick intake checklist (what we need from your team this week):
1) Public and private CIDR ranges for the site + any reserved subnets for future racks
2) List of permitted egress IPs for NAT (or confirmation you want Redwood-managed egress)
3) BGP ASN and a sample peer config if you prefer BGP for cross-connects
4) Storage profile: LUN capacity & IOPS, NVMe cache size, expected working set sizes by model (peak inference QPS)
5) Rack map (which hosts are GPU-capable) and a rough hardware inventory (CPU, RAM, NVMe sizes)
6) Compliance asks: any additional audit logging retention beyond default 90 days

Draft Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): Intake answers + final network diagram (Akash)
- Week 1: Redwood provides site-specific cluster topology proposal (node profiles, control plane placement, kube-proxy strategy)
- Week 2: Security & network pull (collect firewall rules, NAT egress, BGP session test)
- Week 3: Storage integration test plan + dry-run attach/format on a staging host (no production data)
- Week 4: Cutover window scheduling and runbook handoff

Attachments: I prepared a MAP spreadsheet and a compact checklist. Taking a look now, Marissa — any immediate concerns on the proposed timeline?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if that accelerates things.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0192

Attachment: MAP_DataMetric_v2.xlsx (Mutual Action Plan)

Ben / Akash — reviewed the diagram and Ben's checklist. A few technical clarifications that will change nodepool and storage recommendations: 

1) Control plane placement: If you require zero external access to API servers, we'll propose an ingress gateway in the perimeter VPC and keep the API behind a private endpoint with a site-to-site VPN for admin access. Confirm if the colo team can support an IPsec tunnel terminated to an on-prem firewall.

2) Node segmentation: recommend three node pools — gpu-workloads, cpu-batch, and infra (kube-system + logging/metrics). For GPU pool, specify preferred GPU models & per-host GPU count; if you only have a small NVMe shelf per rack, we will bias larger ephemeral scratch on gpu nodes and rely on LUN-backed blockstore for model artifacts.

3) Storage QoS: LUN IOPS are the gating factor. Please provide 95th-percentile IOPS per model inference at target QPS. If you cannot provide fine-grained numbers, supply a conservative number (e.g., 10k IOPS per rack) and we will size caching accordingly.

4) Egress policy: Redwood can operate with either customer-managed NAT egress (preferred for IP allowlisting) or manage egress from a dedicated outbound NAT in our control plane. If you choose customer-managed, we'll need the exact egress IPs before Week 2 tests.

5) Evacuation and rack drain: to meet your target of <2h degraded performance, we recommend maintaining a 1.3x headroom on GPU capacity per failure domain and pre-warm k8s scheduling constraints for fast reprovisioning.

Next steps: Akash — if you can drop the CIDRs, egress IPs, and a short GPU inventory (model + count) into the MAP spreadsheet by Friday, Neha and I will convert that into a concrete nodepool recommendation and a runbook snippet for the storage attach test.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- LUN snapshots: if your storage array supports fast snapshots, enable one so we can validate that model artifact restores are <10 minutes in worst case.
